purpose: This medication is used to treat a rare heart condition called transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). This happens when an unstable protein in your body breaks apart and builds up in your heart, making it stiff and harder to pump blood. Tafamidis helps slow down the damage this causes to your heart.
how_it_works: Your body makes a protein called transthyretin (TTR) that normally carries certain vitamins and hormones in your blood. In people with this condition, TTR becomes unstable and falls apart, forming clumps that deposit in the heart. Tafamidis works by binding to this protein and holding it together so it stays stable and does not break apart and damage your heart.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well. Some side effects that have been reported include urinary tract infections, diarrhea, and upper respiratory infections like colds. These are generally mild for most patients.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as this medicine may harm an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant should use reliable birth control while taking this medication. Always let your doctor know about all other medications and supplements you take, as some drugs may interact with tafamidis.
typical_dosing: The usual dose of Vyndamax (tafamidis) is one 61 mg capsule taken by mouth once daily. The usual dose of Vyndaqel (tafamidis meglumine) is four 20 mg soft gel capsules taken by mouth once daily. Both forms are swallowed whole and can be taken with or without food.
